findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/managed-host-run-smoke.ts:634-647 is ~50% flaky (measured 4 PASS / 4 FAIL over 8 isolated runs), and it is the SOLE verificationEvidence command for 8 must-intents (CHK-001:happy:0, CHK-001:happy:1, CHK-001:edge:0, CHK-001:edge:1, CHK-001:adversarial:0, CHK-001:adversarial:1, CHK-001:adversarial:2, CHK-007:edge:1). The 'deadline-granted-without-provider-identity' case submits with deadlineMs=40 and an in-process runner that wedges, then asserts replacementSafe===false. The fixture permits two interleavings that are BOTH legitimate in production: (a) the worker reaches the launch fence first -> providerLaunchState='granted' -> wedges with providerIdentity=null -> reconciler selects AMBIGUOUS_PROCESS_CLEANUP -> replacementSafe=false (assertion passes); (b) the next-touch reconciler's fenceLaunchBeforeTerminal() flips providerLaunchState 'pending'->'revoked' first -> reconciler selects REAPED_WITHOUT_SIGNAL (reaped:true, residualProcessGroup:false) -> cleanupIsReplacementSafe returns true -> replacementSafe=true (assertion FAILS). I confirmed path (b) directly with a probe: pre-seal snapshot showed launchState=revoked, providerIdentity=null in 4/4 runs, each sealing replacementSafe=true. IMPORTANT SEVERITY QUALIFIER: this is a TEST defect, not a production defect. The launch fence at packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:1355-1367 runs under withTerminalAuthorityLock, so a worker observing 'revoked' provably refuses to spawn any provider; therefore replacementSafe=true is HONEST in that interleaving and the CHK-001:adversarial:1 honesty property holds in shipped code. The reliable sibling case at managed-host-run-smoke.ts:807-858 tests the same property correctly by spawning a REAL worker process (--granted-no-identity-worker) instead of using the in-process seam. Impact on this review lane: the recorded result:'pass' evidence for all 7 CHK-001 must-intents plus CHK-007:edge:1 rests on a coin-flip rather than a deterministic assertion, so those intents are not reliably covered. Suggested fix: make the fixture deterministic (e.g. confirm providerLaunchState==='granted' before allowing the deadline to elapse, mirroring the line-807 sibling) rather than changing production replacementSafe semantics.
